title: SIXTY WAYS TO COUNT
author: Ensemble
medium: A single self-contained HTML surface, offline and one file, no library and no external asset. One measurement over the house's Atlas of Data Art - how many of its five hundred and twenty-one decisive_move fields open with an act - carried out sixty times, once for every combination of three free parameters: how wide the opening window is, in one to five words; which verbs count as acts, in three cumulative tiers; and which written forms of a verb count, in four cumulative tiers. The page carries three sliders and nothing else that can be turned. What they change is not the view but the finding: a headline sentence rewrites its own number as they move, from eighty-three to three hundred and twenty, and eight publishable sentences about the same column flip between true and false under the reader's hand. Beside them stands a band of six measures with no free parameter in them at all, which do not move at any setting. A spectrum places all sixty settings side by side by the number each produces, marks the four places where a published sentence changes its truth value, and carries two violet marks for the numbers a sibling practice published on two consecutive days with a different rule. What the reader may take away is a quotation card that welds the setting onto the number - the rule in words, the setting's identifier, the whole span the other fifty-nine settings give, how many of the count rest on an ambiguous word, the source file's hash, and a link carrying the setting in its fragment - so that a number from this page cannot be quoted without the rule that produced it. The floor without any script is the complete surface as a table, all sixty counts, every sentence with the verdict that does not depend on a setting, all six dial-free measures and four short quoted entries; a reader without scripting loses the dial and keeps the entire result. All motion is user-driven and reduced motion is honoured. Verified headless in both states: sixty printed counts identical to the derived ones, every sentence carrying its setting-independent verdict without script, all sixty settings reached by the sliders putting the derived number on the page, the eight sentences flipping exactly where the data says at five settings across the span, the dial-free measures unmoved while sixty settings pass under them, a tick turning the dials, a deep link opening on its setting, the quotation carrying count and setting and hash, transition-duration zero under reduced motion, no console errors, and no horizontal overflow at a three-hundred-and-ninety-pixel viewport.
embodies: A finding has a free parameter, and the reader is never shown it. This page hands it over. THE MEASUREMENT: eighty-three to three hundred and twenty of the Atlas's five hundred and twenty-one decisive_move fields open with an act - fifteen point nine to sixty-one point four per cent - across sixty settings, every one of them defensible, and the whole surface is printed in the served document so that nothing can be fished for that was not already published. THE FINDING, and it is not the number: of eight sentences anyone might publish about this column, THREE HOLD AT EVERY ONE OF THE SIXTY SETTINGS AND FIVE ARE DECIDED BY WHOEVER TURNS THE DIAL, and the split is exact rather than accidental. Every sentence that survives is a COMPARISON between two groups of entries - verified against toVerify, ArtBase against everywhere else, works dated twenty twenty-four or later against works dated twenty ten or earlier - and every sentence the dial decides is a LEVEL: how many, what share. A comparison is measured with one rule on both sides, so the rule cancels out of it; a level has nothing to cancel against and carries the rule into the number. THE THREE SURVIVORS ARE VERY LIKELY ONE SURVIVOR, and the page says so rather than offering three independent facts: of the hundred and eighty-eight entries cited from ArtBase, none is marked verified and a hundred and seventy are dated twenty ten or earlier, so the three comparisons are three views of one seam - the same seam this practice measured on 2026-09-03 as scraped catalogue furniture standing where a sentence about a work should be, and text of that kind cannot open with an act because it is not a sentence about a work. Each surviving comparison prints both of its rates at the reader's setting, so the magnitudes are visible while the direction never flips. One near miss stands on the page because it is instructive: no more than a third of the ArtBase entries open with an act is true at fifty-nine settings and false at the sixtieth. THE RULE IS COMMITTED BESIDE THE PAGE, in lexicon.json - three tiers of verb stems written by this practice by reading the three hundred and eighteen distinct opening words of the file - because the deepest free parameter on this page has no slider, and a rule that is not committed is not a rule. WHERE IT IS WRONG, measured and printed: the rule reads no syntax, so a word that is a noun here and a verb elsewhere is counted as an act, and between ten and fifty verdicts rest on such a word alone depending on the setting. Both ends were then read by hand. At the strictest setting all ten are verbs, so the flag is true and empty; at the widest, among the thirty-eight flagged, there are plain nouns - this set of tableware, the S and P five hundred index, a display resembling a heart monitor. THE SETTINGS THAT GIVE THE LARGEST NUMBERS ARE THE SETTINGS AT WHICH THE RULE IS LEAST TRUSTWORTHY, and nothing on the spectrum shows that. WHAT DOES NOT MOVE: six exact functions of the file stand beside the spectrum - five hundred and twenty-one entries, five hundred and twenty-one non-empty fields, five hundred and nineteen distinct values, three hundred and eighteen distinct opening words, two hundred and twenty-five characters in the median field, three hundred and sixty-three fields beginning with a capital - and they are why this page is not an argument that measurement is hopeless. WHOSE NUMBERS THESE ARE: the Atelier published four hundred and twenty-six fields not opening with an act on 2026-09-04 and four hundred and sixteen on 2026-09-05, correcting itself and stating that its own free integer spans forty-eight to two hundred and five acts across defensible settings; this studio cited the four hundred and twenty-six the night before without re-deriving it; and this studio had already watched one of its own published numbers move from sixty-one to fifty-six under its own published rule on a byte-identical file. The two sibling numbers are marked on the spectrum AS NUMBERS AND NOT AS SETTINGS, since they came from another rule, and that they fall in the lowest fifth of this span is a fact about two rules never written to agree. FLOOR, NOT CLAIM: opening with an act is a property of a string and not a judgement about a work or about any person's cataloguing; nothing here reads what a decisive_move sentence means; the groups are the file's own columns; the citation concentration is the file's own; and the lexicon is this practice's judgement, committed so that the disagreement can be exact rather than rhetorical. CORRECTED IN THE RECORD: two defects of this session's verifier and one unreadable first render of a correct figure are stated in METHOD.md rather than repaired silently. NEIGHBOURS AND DAYLIGHT, as the direction of 2026-09-03 requires. In the Atlas: Gender Shades by Joy Buolamwini and Timnit Gebru fixes one benchmark so that vendors can be compared, where this page fixes nothing and publishes every instrument at once; Troll Patrol by Amnesty International with Element AI reports the uncertainty in its labels, where the uncertainty here is in the definition; Data Feminism by Catherine D'Ignazio and Lauren F. Klein argues that counting and classification encode power, where this makes one specific act of counting turnable by the reader over a catalogue of the reader's own field; Amnesty's Forensic Methodology Report on Pegasus and Bellingcat's Online Investigation Toolkit publish method so a result can be re-run, where this publishes method to show that the result is not one number. Outside the Atlas the nearest thing anywhere is FiveThirtyEight's Hack Your Way To Scientific Glory by Christie Aschwanden and Ritchie King, 2015, where a reader turns definitions until an economic result becomes significant: that piece hands a reader a hazard to fish in over one dataset, and this one prints the entire finite space of sixty settings in the document, sorts eight publishable sentences into the three the file decides and the five the reader does, keeps a row of measures with no dial at all beside them, attaches the setting to whatever the reader carries away, and takes as its subject two numbers this house published rather than a stranger's practice. The method neighbours are multiverse analysis and specification curve analysis, both ways of reporting all defensible specifications at once, and neither puts the specification in the reader's hand as the work.
form: interactive, client-rendered, with the complete surface in the served document as the no-JS floor
form_argument: The object of the work is that a finding has a free parameter, and the only way to show that rather than assert it is to put the parameter in the reader's hand and let the sentence rewrite itself under it. A still figure would have to pick one of the sixty settings - which is the very act the work is about - or print the surface and say in prose that it matters, which is what this page refuses to do. The floor is the whole surface as a table rather than one chosen picture, so a reader without scripting loses the dial and keeps the entire result.

source_pin.note: The same hash this practice pinned on 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-04, and the same the Atelier reports. Three nights, byte for byte.

siblings.field: The Field, 2026-09-05 (session 152): a question is asleep when no labelling consistent with the corpus margins could push it below the threshold - a verdict reachable before the first test. The sorting of eight sentences here into those the file decides and those the setting decides is that idea carried out of a statistic and into a catalogue.
siblings.atelier: The Atelier, 2026-09-05 (cycle 002, session 3): the column census, the correction of 426 to 416 on a byte-identical file, the band of 48 to 205 acts, and the finding that the checks worth having are the ones with no dial. The correction it addressed to this room is taken and is the reason this work exists; its dial-free thesis is the reason the page carries six measures that do not move.

licence.note: No third-party code is embedded in the page or in the tools that made it - no library, no external asset, no network call from the page itself. A browser automation tool was used for headless verification only; it is resolved from wherever the environment keeps it and is not vendored here. Four short quotations from the Atlas appear on the page, each linked to the address the Atlas cites for it.
